A culture of responsibility and self discipline

The Masculine Strategy Initiative (MASC) is an inter-community youth empowerment network founded by Victor Oodo, Head Boy (2024–2025) of Federal Science and Technical College (FTC), Yaba, Lagos. It was built for the developmental needs of young adolescent boys, joining peer-to-senior mentorship, technical trade readiness, physical wellbeing and leadership discipline.

Through mentorship tracks and hands-on skill workshops, MASC equips rising male students with the character and practical tools to thrive in higher education and vocational careers.

Built on the Sustainable Development Goals

Each MASC pillar lines up with a United Nations goal, so every activity has a measurable purpose.

SDG 4 · Quality Education

Study together

Peer study circles, evening prep accountability and tutoring so junior members excel in STEM, technical drawing and general academics.

SDG 8 · Decent Work & Growth

Learn a trade early

Acting prefects and student mentors in electrical installation, mechanical engineering, computer craft, bookkeeping, printing and fabrication build workplace readiness.

SDG 10 & 16 · Equality, Peace & Institutions

Lead with respect

Constructive student governance, active anti-bullying enforcement and Model United Nations prepare boys for civic leadership.

SDG 3 · Good Health & Well-being

Stay strong

Inter-house athletics, physical conditioning, hostel sanitation campaigns and support networks with school clinic prefects.

Five guilds, one brotherhood

Every junior is paired with an acting prefect or student mentor whose strengths match his interests and career track.

STEM & Technical Trades

Solar tech, embedded systems (Arduino/ESP32), electrical wiring, computer craft and drafting. Supports SDG 4 & 8.

Mentors: Friday Goodnews, Udaewah Teriloluwa, Dawodu Iduwaleyi, Igwe Caleb

Sports & Wellness

Track and field, basketball, volleyball, fitness and sports science. Supports SDG 3.

Mentors: Gabriel Daniel, Akande Kehinde, Akpoguma Dominion, Pyne Noah

Civic Leadership

Anti-bullying leadership, Model UN, public speaking and student governance. Supports SDG 10 & 16.

Mentors: Onyemi Ibukunoluwa, Ishola Alim, Lawal Oluwadamilare, Agbazue Solomon

Creative Arts & Media

Solo and ensemble drumming, radio and TV broadcasting, graphic design and visual arts. Supports SDG 4.

Mentors: Akpoguma Dominion, Anyanwu Chukwuadi

Business & Finance

Commercial math, bookkeeping, salesmanship and entrepreneurship. Supports SDG 8.

Mentors: Adeprosy Samuel, Amarfula Daniel, Shaibu Mustapha

A note for parents and guardians

Every junior member is registered with a named acting prefect or student mentor and a clear career-growth track.

Welcome to the Masculine Strategy Initiative mentorship program.

Your son is part of a structured network founded to build character, academic excellence, technical skills and leadership discipline in adolescent boys.

He is paired with an acting prefect or student mentor who guides him in academic goal setting, health, hostel discipline and technical skill growth. Follow his progress and our updates on the official channels below, and contact the MASC Secretariat with any question.

Warm regards,
Victor Oodo, President & Founder, MASC
